new.title: Tenecteplase, alteplase, and endovascular thrombectomy in extended-window acute ischemic stroke with intracranial large-vessel occlusion: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE] The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations. [METHODS] We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). new.title: Exploratory topological modeling of reported frequencies of aortic arch branching variations.
new.abstract: Anatomical variations in the branching patterns of the aortic arch affect endovascular access, surgical planning, and cerebral perfusion strategies. However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies. Seven pooled type-level frequency estimates from a published meta-analysis were analyzed. Node-Shift and Edge-Loss-Change Scores were defined from the final branching topology relative to Type 1 (separate brachiocephalic, left common carotid, and left subclavian origins from a left-sided arch). new.title: Pre-stroke functional status and prognosis following mechanical thrombectomy: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: IntroductionMechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an endovascular approach applicable to large- and medium-vessel occlusion in the context of ischemic stroke (IS), with recanalization rates superior to 80% and favorable clinical outcomes. However, its benefits in patients with pre-existing functional disability remain unclear because these individuals are typically excluded from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). This systematic review and meta-analysis therefore aimed to assess how pre-stroke functional status influences key prognostic outcomes after MT.MethodologyPubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases were searched for English studies published from inception to September 2025. new.title: PD-1/ PD-l1 Inhibitors and Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Brain Metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [PURPOSE] Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is the treatment of choice for limited brain metastases (BM), and its combination with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors is hypothesized to offer synergistic therapeutic benefits. However, there are concerns regarding augmented risk of radiation-induced brain necrosis (RIBN). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the efficacy and toxicity profile of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with SRS or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (FSRT). [METHODS] Four databases were screened, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus from inception to November 2025. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), extracranial and distant intracranial progression free survival (PFS), and local control (LC). new.title: Duration of single-agent perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis and postoperative meningitis after endoscopic endonasal skull base surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,981 patients.
new.abstract: Postoperative meningitis is a rare but serious complication in endoscopic-endonasal skull-base surgery. Although prophylactic antibiotics are routinely administered, the optimal regimen and duration remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the incidence of meningitis and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage associated with single-agent perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched through February 2025. Eligible studies reported postoperative meningitis or intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak after endoscopic endonasal skull-base surgery using a single primary prophylactic antibiotic. new.title: Symptom duration and postoperative outcomes in degenerative cervical myelopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Surgical decompression is regarded as standard treatment for degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM). However, the timing of surgery remains a critical yet unresolved issue in clinical practice. Therefore, this meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of symptom duration on surgical outcomes and determine the optimal timing for surgery. [METHODS] A systematic search was conducted on 16th November 2025 using PubMed, Ovid, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify eligible articles. Studies comprising patients with DCM undergoing surgery, assessing outcome by mJOA score at a minimum of 12 months of follow-up, were included. new.title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
new.abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. new.title: The perspective of combining pulsed field ablation and left atrial appendage closure.
new.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) are increasingly discussed as complementary strategies in atrial fibrillation (AF) care, addressing rhythm control and long-term thromboembolic risk. The rationale is attractive, but the current evidence base is uneven. Randomized evidence for LAAC around AF ablation is strongest for thermal-ablation-era workflows, particularly the OPTION trial, which showed lower non-procedure-related major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with LAAC than with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and non-inferiority for death, stroke, or systemic embolism. new.title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface.
new.abstract: Brain activation to verbal commands can be detected by EEG in clinically unresponsive patients. These patients with cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) are unable to communicate with the environment despite preserved consciousness. Advanced brain-computer interfaces (BCI) are promising to support motor function in patients with motor neuron disease or spinal cord injury. Our primary objective was to determine if clinically unresponsive patients can control a self-paced, one-way BCI early after acute brain injury. Secondarily, we assessed the association of BCI control with short- and long-term outcomes. new.title: The macaque IT cortex but not current artificial vision networks encode object position in perceptually aligned coordinates.
new.abstract: Efficient interaction with the visual world requires not only object identification but also localization of where objects are in space. While spatial ("where") processing has classically been attributed to dorsal stream pathways, recent work has shown that object position can also be decoded from ventral stream responses, including the inferior temporal (IT) cortex. However, because object position in these paradigms is coupled to pixel-based location, it has remained unclear whether ventral stream position signals are perceptually meaningful or instead reflect incidental inheritance from retinotopic inputs. new.title: ACF-Net: Design of an adaptive cross-modal fusion network for cross-subject wearable EEG-EMG gesture recognition.
new.abstract: Cross-subject gesture recognition in wearable brain-computer interfaces is constrained by four structural deficiencies: symmetric cross-modal attention discarding cortical precedence over muscular execution, priors confined to post hoc analysis, invariance anchored on unimodal features, and adaptation requiring labelled target-domain data. This study closes these gaps by embedding corticomuscular coupling directly into the network architecture rather than recovering it from data.Approach: ACF-Net is a four-stage pipeline embedding neurophysiological priors directly into fusion. new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] To develop and validate a compact Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)-enabled wearable functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) device for real-time hemodynamic monitoring and proposes a task-evoked metric for identifying transient oxygenation events during cognitive engagement. [METHOD] We designed a four-channel wearable fNIRS biosensor that integrates optical sensing, signal acquisition, and wireless transmission into a compact, cable-free platform using off-the-shelf electronic components. The device was characterized through optical power linearity, ADC voltage input, pulsed light acquisition, and signal-to-noise ratio analysis. new.title: EEG-VTSFN: An enhanced approach for differentiating between unipolar and bipolar mood disorders.
new.abstract: Accurate differentiation between Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Unipolar Depression (UD) is a significant clinical challenge due to overlapping manifestations and a lack of objective biomarkers. While EEG offers high temporal resolution, its psychiatric utility for diagnostic differentiation remains limited. To address this, we propose the Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based Time-Space Fusion Network (VTSFN). VTSFN transforms complex EEG signals into latent-space representations to mitigate noise and construct stable latent co-activation patterns. By integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms, the model captures temporal dynamics to identify discriminative patterns. new.title: DCDA-Net: A depthwise convolution dilated attention network with temporal weighted loss for seizure prediction.
new.abstract: The sudden and unforeseeable nature of seizures poses serious threats to patients' safety and quality of daily life, making the development of highly accurate and reliable seizure prediction methods of significant clinical importance. To this end, this study proposed a seizure prediction model by integrating depthwise convolution and a novel dilated attention mechanism, named DCDA-Net. Depthwise convolution was first employed to extract features from each EEG channel independently, preserving spatial channel information for subsequent seizure evolution analysis. Innovatively combining dilated convolution with self-attention mechanisms, a dilated attention module was devised to efficiently capture long-range temporal dependencies. new.title: Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer for multimodal EEG-fMRI learning in ADHD diagnosis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is associated with distributed alterations in large-scale brain systems, making reliable diagnosis from neuroimaging data challenging. EEG-derived and fMRI-derived static functional-connectivity profiles summarize patterns of electrophysiological coupling and hemodynamic covariation, respectively, but their heterogeneous signal mechanisms make direct multimodal alignment difficult. [NEW METHOD] We propose a Cross-Modal Masked Connectome Transformer (CM-MCT) for EEG-fMRI based ADHD diagnosis. new.title: Deep learning algorithms for predicting intraoperative hypotension: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with myocardial injury, acute kidney injury, perioperative stroke, and 30-day mortality. Deep learning (DL) refers to a family of machine-learning methods that learn multiple levels of data representation through nonlinear transformations. In perioperative monitoring, DL models can learn patterns from time-varying physiological signals and combine them with clinical variables to estimate impending IOH risk. DL algorithms applied to continuous physiological waveforms therefore represent a rapidly expanding paradigm for early IOH prediction, but their pooled diagnostic accuracy has not been synthesised within a unified diagnostic-accuracy framework. new.title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [AIMS] Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance. [METHODS AND RESULTS] A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. new.title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
new.abstract: This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. new.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly being integrated into nutrition care and dietary counseling. Evaluating their usefulness, accuracy, and limitations is essential before widespread clinical adoption.AimTo systematically review the evidence on the performance of ChatGPT and related AI tools in nutrition and dietetics, including comparisons with other AI models and human experts.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and included studies published until February 2025. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remains a frequent and devastating event, and conventional early warning scores (EWSs) coupled with rapid response systems (RRSs) have shown inconsistent effects on patient-centered outcomes, largely owing to limited predictive accuracy and high false-alarm burden. AI-based EWSs (AI-EWSs) have demonstrated superior discrimination retrospectively, but high-quality prospective evidence in true external validation environments remains scarce. Existing AI-EWS trials have either been confined to internal-development settings or bundled the algorithm with specific implementation infrastructure, leaving the stand-alone effect of AI-based software as a medical device (AI-SaMD) on patient outcomes uncharacterized. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES] Many spinal imaging reports are written above recommended health literacy levels, limiting patient comprehension at a time when rapid electronic access to radiology results is increasing. We aim to evaluate whether supplemental natural language processing (NLP)-modified radiology reports-within the context of usual patient portal access to the original report-are associated with improved patient-reported perceived understandability compared with standard reports among patients undergoing spine imaging. new.title: Multicenter external validation of a multimodal MRI deep-learning model to predict meningioma bone invasion.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Preoperative detection of meningioma bone invasion lacks objective biomarkers and relies on subjective radiological assessment, posing a risk of excessive bone resection or residual tumor. We therefore developed and externally validated a parsimonious six-feature DenseNet121 signature derived from multiparametric MRI across two independent institutions. [METHODS] In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 438 consecutive patients (mean age, 53 ± 11 years; 77% women) with histologically confirmed meningioma were allocated to training (n = 182), internal validation (n = 77), and external test (n = 179) sets. new.title: Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies. [METHODS] We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Ablation procedures are frequently used to restore sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation (AF), given the increased stroke risk associated with AF. The decision to discontinue oral anticoagulation (OAC) therapy postprocedure requires careful consideration of stroke and bleeding risks, especially because of the absence of definitive guidelines. [OBJECTIVE] This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the implications of OAC discontinuation after catheter ablation for AF, focusing on thromboembolic events (TEs) and bleeding events. [METHODS] A systematic search was conducted in 4 databases for studies comparing OAC discontinuation with maintenance in patients with AF postablation. ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] The Evolut Low Risk trial enrolled patients with severe aortic stenosis at low surgical risk. [OBJECTIVES] Our prespecified objective was to report the 6-year clinical outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) vs surgery from the Evolut Low Risk trial. ns.title: IVUS-Guided versus Angiography-Guided PCI in Unprotected Left Main Coronary Disease.
ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is increasingly used for revascularization of unprotected left main coronary artery disease. Whether intravascular ultrasonographic (IVUS) guidance during PCI results in better clinical outcomes than conventional angiographic guidance alone is uncertain. [METHODS] In an international, multicenter, open-label trial, we randomly assigned patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either IVUS-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI. The primary end point was a patient-oriented composite of any stroke, any myocardial infarction, any revascularization, or death from any cause at the longest follow-up. ns.title: The Safety and Outcomes of Elective Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in the Elderly: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis.
ns.abstract: [PURPOSE] Prevalence of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) increases with age. Previous trials confirm that elective endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an effective intervention for AAA. However, few elderly patients were recruited into randomized trials, whereas in contemporary clinical practice, elective repair is commonly performed on octogenarians. We evaluated the safety and outcome of elective EVAR in elderly patients to inform clinical practice and vascular service provision. [METHODS] A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting risk of complications and death in patients undergoing elective EVAR was performed (PROSPERO CRD: 42022308423). bmi.title: Technical system of electroencephalography-based brain-computer interface: Advances, applications, and challenges.
bmi.abstract: Electroencephalography-based brain-computer interfaces have revolutionized the integration of neural signals with technological systems, offering transformative solutions across neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical practice. This review systematically analyzes advancements in electroencephalography-based brain-computer interface architectures, emphasizing four pillars, namely signal acquisition, paradigm design, decoding algorithms, and diverse applications. The aim is to bridge the gap between technology and application and guide future research. In signal acquisition, noninvasive systems using wet, dry, and semi-dry electrodes are more comfortable and gentler on the skin compared to traditional methods. bmi.abstract: Previous research has demonstrated the potential of using pre-trained language models for decoding open vocabulary Electroencephalography (EEG) signals captured through a non-invasive Brain-Computer Interface (BCI). However, the impact of embedding EEG signals in the context of language models and the effect of subjectivity, remain unexplored, leading to uncertainty about the best approach to enhance decoding performance. Additionally, current evaluation metrics used to assess decoding effectiveness are predominantly syntactic and do not provide insights into the comprehensibility of the decoded output for human understanding. ai.title: Epicardial and pericardial adipose tissue: anatomy, physiology, imaging, segmentation, and treatment effects.
ai.abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. We sought to discuss the currently used imaging modalities to assess these fat compartments-CT, MRI, and echocardiography-emphasizing their advantages, limitations, and the urgent need for standardization for both scanning and image reconstruction. ai.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent.
ai.abstract: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni's action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. ai.title: A deep learning framework for efficient pathology image analysis.
ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed digital pathology by enabling biomarker prediction from high-resolution whole-slide images. However, current methods are computationally inefficient, processing thousands of redundant tiles per slide and requiring complex aggregation models. We introduce EAGLE (Efficient Approach for Guided Local Examination), a deep learning framework that emulates pathologists by selectively analyzing informative regions. EAGLE combines task-agnostic tile selection with detailed feature extraction and is benchmarked against leading slide- and tile-level foundation models across 43 tasks from nine cancer types spanning morphology, biomarker prediction, treatment response and prognosis. ai.title: Deep learning electrocardiogram model for risk stratification of coronary revascularization need in the emergency department.
ai.abstract: [BACKGROUND AND AIMS] Identification of patients with acute coronary syndrome requiring coronary revascularization can be challenging due to inconclusive electrocardiogram (ECG) findings or biomarker results. A deep learning model to detect ECG patterns associated with revascularization likelihood was developed, aiming to guide further assessment and reduce diagnostic uncertainty. [METHODS] A convolutional neural network model was trained on 144 691 ED visits from a US cohort (60 ± 19 years; 53% female; 0.6% revascularization), tested on a separate test cohort (n = 35 995), and benchmarked against clinician ECG interpretation and cardiac troponin T (TnT). ai.title: Foundation models for radiology: fundamentals, applications, opportunities, challenges, risks, and prospects.
ai.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) represent a significant evolution in artificial intelligence (AI), impacting diverse fields. Within radiology, this evolution offers greater adaptability, multimodal integration, and improved generalizability compared with traditional narrow AI. Utilizing large-scale pre-training and efficient fine-tuning, FMs can support diverse applications, including image interpretation, report generation, integrative diagnostics combining imaging with clinical/laboratory data, and synthetic data creation, holding significant promise for advancements in precision medicine. ai.title: Human versus artificial intelligence: evaluating ChatGPT's performance in conducting published systematic reviews with meta-analysis in chronic pain research.
ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large-language models like Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), has demonstrated potential in streamlining research methodologies. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses, often considered the pinnacle of evidence-based medicine, are inherently time-intensive and demand meticulous planning, rigorous data extraction, thorough analysis, and careful synthesis. Despite promising applications of AI, its utility in conducting systematic reviews with meta-analysis remains unclear. This study evaluated ChatGPT's accuracy in conducting key tasks of a systematic review with meta-analysis.
